title: Quotients by initial parts of a system of parameters have the expected dimension
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer equal to its Krull dimension $\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in\mathfrak m$ generate an ideal $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ with $\sqrt J=\mathfrak m$, where $\sqrt J=\{b\in A:b^N\in J\text{ for some integer }N\geq1\}$. Then for every integer $i$ with $1\leq i\leq d$ one has $\dim\bigl(A/(a_1,\ldots,a_i)\bigr)=d-i$; quotient rings have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: Tag 02IE, lemma-elements-generate-ideal-definition (lines 14712–14718); ideal of definition means radical equal to the maximal ideal, Definition Tag 07DU, definition-ideal-definition (lines 14019–14024).

proof.text: Fix $i$ with $1\le i\le d$, and put $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$, $B=A/I$, $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/I$. By [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $q$ is surjective with kernel $I$. Ideals $L\subset B$ correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $I$: the inverse maps are $L\mapsto q^{-1}L$ and $H\mapsto q(H)$, since $q^{-1}q(H)=H$ when $I\subset H$. The product test for primality shows this correspondence preserves prime ideals and strict inclusions. It also preserves maximal ideals, so $B$ is nonzero local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$; here $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ is proper. For each $L$, finite generators of $q^{-1}L$ map to finite generators of $L$, proving $B$ Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Every prime chain in $B$ lifts to one in $A$, so $0\le e:=\dim B\le d$, using [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In a local ring every prime lies in its unique maximal ideal, hence the height of that maximal ideal, defined as the supremum of lengths of prime chains ending below it, equals the ring dimension. In particular $\operatorname{ht}_A(\mathfrak m)=d$ and $\operatorname{ht}_B(\mathfrak n)=e$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $R=A$, $t=i$, $f_j=a_j$ for $1\le j\le i$, and $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak m$. The ring is Noetherian, $\mathfrak m$ is prime because it is maximal, and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Its quotient prime is $\mathfrak n$. The height identifications in Step 1 give $d\le e+i$.

proof.text: In $B$, put $K=(q(a_{i+1}),\ldots,q(a_d))$, with $K=(0)$ if $i=d$, and put $C=B/K$. The surjection $A\to C$, $a\mapsto q(a)\bmod K$, has kernel $J$: membership of $q(a)$ in $K$ means that $a$ differs from a linear combination of $a_{i+1},\ldots,a_d$ by an element of $I$. Thus $C\cong A/J$, and $C\ne0$ since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. If a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ contains $J$, then for each $b\in\mathfrak m=\sqrt J$ a power $b^N$ belongs to $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$; repeated primality gives $b\in\mathfrak p$. Hence $\mathfrak m\subseteq\mathfrak p$, and maximality gives $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$. By the prime correspondence proved in Step 1, $C$ therefore has exactly one prime ideal, namely $\mathfrak n/K$. There are no strict inclusions of prime ideals in $C$, so $\dim C=0$ by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Its unique prime has height zero for the same reason.

source.place: Tag 02IE, lemma-elements-generate-ideal-definition, proof via repeated one-equation bounds of Tag 00KW, lemma-one-equation; the bound for a finite list is the cited height-quotient lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $R=B$, $t=d-i$, $f_1,\ldots,f_t=q(a_{i+1}),\ldots,q(a_d)$, and $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak n$. Step 1 established that $B$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, hence prime. Every listed generator lies in $\mathfrak n$, and the generated ideal is $K$. The image prime is $\mathfrak n/K$, of height zero by Step 3. Thus $e=\operatorname{ht}_B(\mathfrak n)\le0+(d-i)=d-i$. The cited lemma includes $t=0$, so this application also covers $i=d$.

source.place: Tag 02IE, lemma-elements-generate-ideal-definition, proof via repeated one-equation bounds of Tag 00KW, lemma-one-equation; the bound for a finite list is the cited height-quotient lemma.

proof.text: Combining $d\le e+i$ from Step 2 with $e\le d-i$ from Step 4, and using that $d,e,i$ are finite integers, gives $e=d-i$. Since $B=A/(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$, this is the required equality. If $d=0$ there is no $i$ in the stated range, so the assertion is vacuous.
